tree.title: Neonatal Respiratory Distress — Initial Evaluation & Management
tree.subtitle: For Level II / Level II+ Nurseries and Rural Emergency Departments

population.description: Term and near-term neonates (≥34 weeks GA) presenting with signs of respiratory distress within the first 6 hours of life, evaluated in a Level II nursery or rural ED.
exclusions: Gestational age < 34 weeks (refer to NICU protocol)
Known congenital heart disease prior to evaluation

guideline_sources.title: Management of Neonates Born at 34 0/7 to 36 6/7 Weeks Gestation
2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Neonatal Resuscitation

tree.clinical_disclaimer: This clinical decision support tool is a reference aid only and does not replace clinical judgment. Always verify against current institutional protocols. Consult a neonatologist or transfer to higher level of care when indicated.

RDS.definition: Surfactant-deficiency lung disease of preterm/near-term infants causing progressive hypoxemia, decreased lung compliance, and characteristic bilateral ground-glass opacification on CXR.
RDS.extended_notes: RDS is the most common cause of respiratory failure in premature infants. Peak incidence at 34–36 weeks GA. Surfactant replacement therapy has dramatically reduced mortality.

TTN.definition: Delayed clearance of fetal lung fluid causing transient respiratory distress in term/near-term infants. Self-limited, typically resolves within 24–72 hours.
TTN.extended_notes: TTN is associated with cesarean delivery (lack of thoracic squeeze), maternal diabetes, and sedation. CXR shows central haziness and fluid in fissures (wet lung). Treatment is supportive.

Downes-score.definition: Validated neonatal respiratory distress scoring tool (0–10). Score 0–3: mild; 4–6: moderate; ≥7: severe/impending failure. Assesses respiratory rate, retractions, grunting, air entry, and cyanosis.

CPAP.definition: Non-invasive respiratory support delivering a constant distending pressure to maintain alveolar recruitment and functional residual capacity (FRC) in spontaneously breathing neonates.
CPAP.extended_notes: Starting pressure 5–6 cmH2O for near-term infants with RDS. Increase FiO2 to maintain SpO2 90–95%.

FiO2.definition: The proportion of oxygen in the inspired gas mixture. Room air = 0.21 (21%). Express as a decimal (0.21–1.0) or percentage (21–100%).

surfactant.definition: Phospholipid mixture administered intratracheally to replace deficient endogenous surfactant in RDS. Natural/animal-derived preparations (beractant, poractant alfa) are preferred over synthetic.

INSURE.definition: INtubate-SURfactant-Extubate strategy: brief intubation for surfactant administration followed by prompt extubation to CPAP. Reduces need for prolonged mechanical ventilation.

ref-nrp-2021.citation: Weiner GM, ed. Textbook of Neonatal Resuscitation (NRP), 8th ed. American Academy of Pediatrics; 2021.

ref-aap-late-preterm.citation: AAP Committee on Fetus and Newborn. Management of neonates born at 34 0/7 through 36 6/7 weeks. Pediatrics. 2022;150(6):e2022057990.

ref-downes-1970.citation: Downes JJ, Vidyasagar D, Boggs TR Jr, Morrow GM 3rd. Respiratory distress syndrome of newborn infants. Clin Pediatr (Phila). 1970;9(6):325-331.

ref-insure-cochrane.citation: Schulz MK, et al. Early CPAP versus surfactant in extremely premature infants (SUPPORT). N Engl J Med. 2010;362:1970-1979.

ref-aap-spo2-targets.citation: AAP/AHA. Neonatal resuscitation: 2025 American Heart Association guidelines. Circulation. 2025.

clinical_content.summary: Neonate presenting with one or more signs of respiratory distress. Begin systematic evaluation.

time_constraint.label: Golden first hour
time_constraint.urgency_note: Complete initial assessment within 15 minutes of identifying respiratory distress.

items.point: Most common causes: TTN, RDS, pneumonia/infection, pneumothorax, congenital anomalies.
Obtain preductal SpO2 (right hand) to detect PPHN. Postductal SpO2 (foot) for gradient.
Any neonate with RR > 80 or SpO2 < 85% requires immediate intervention.
Gestational age is the single most important predictor of RDS risk.

items.alert: HR < 100 bpm: Switch to NRP resuscitation algorithm immediately.
Absent breath sounds + shift of heart tones: Consider tension pneumothorax — needle decompression before imaging.

clinical_content.summary: Rapid triage: identify immediate life threats before detailed evaluation.

criteria.label: Apnea episodes (>20 sec or with bradycardia)
Central cyanosis not responding to supplemental O2

items.point: ANY single criterion in this screen mandates immediate intervention — do not await full Downes scoring.
Central cyanosis = bluish discoloration of lips, tongue, mucous membranes. Acrocyanosis (hands/feet only) is normal in the first 24 hours.
Preductal-postductal SpO2 gradient > 10% suggests PPHN — consult neonatologist.

items.alert: If any criterion is met, proceed to IMMEDIATE STABILIZATION before completing this tree.

routing.question: Does the neonate meet ANY immediate life-threat criterion?

branches.label: NO — None met; proceed to detailed scoring

clinical_content.summary: Life-threatening respiratory compromise. Initiate stabilization simultaneously with ongoing assessment.

actions.label: Position: head midline, slight neck extension (sniffing position).
Apply supplemental oxygen — titrate to SpO2 90–95% (preductal).
Initiate continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring and pulse oximetry.
Establish IV or UVC access.
Obtain blood glucose stat — treat hypoglycemia (glucose < 45 mg/dL) immediately.
Notify neonatologist or on-call physician and prepare for possible transfer.
If SpO2 < 85% despite 1.0 FiO2: Initiate CPAP at 5–6 cmH2O.
actions.conditional: SpO2 < 85% despite supplemental O2 at 1.0 FiO2

actions.label: If apnea or respiratory failure: Positive pressure ventilation (PPV) and intubation.
actions.conditional: Apnea, gasping, or SpO2 unresponsive to CPAP

items.point: Target SpO2 90–95% in term/near-term neonates receiving supplemental oxygen.
Avoid hyperoxia: SpO2 > 95% in premature or near-term infants is associated with retinopathy and lung injury.
UVC is preferred IV access in sick neonates — can be placed to 5 cm depth for emergency access.

items.annotation: NRP 8th Ed: oxygen titration targets and CPAP initiation thresholds.
2025 AHA/AAP: updated SpO2 targets in neonatal resuscitation.

items.alert: Do not delay oxygen and CPAP initiation waiting for imaging or labs.
If pneumothorax suspected (asymmetric breath sounds, tracheal deviation): Transillumination or immediate needle decompression before CXR.

clinical_content.summary: Calculate Downes Score (0–10) to quantify severity of respiratory distress and guide management pathway.

criteria.label: Respiratory rate < 60/min = 0 pts; 60–80 = 1 pt; > 80 = 2 pts
criteria.note: Score worst value in past 15 min

criteria.label: Retractions: None = 0; Mild intercostal = 1; Moderate sub+intercostal = 2
Expiratory grunt: None = 0; Audible with stethoscope = 1; Audible at bedside = 2
Air entry: Normal = 0; Decreased = 1; Barely audible = 2
Cyanosis: None = 0; In room air only = 1; In 40% FiO2 = 2

score_thresholds.label: Moderate
score_thresholds.interpretation: Supplemental oxygen; consider CPAP; obtain CXR/CBC/BG

score_thresholds.label: Severe
score_thresholds.interpretation: Impending respiratory failure — CPAP or intubation; transfer consideration

assessment_items.label: Capillary blood gas or arterial blood gas
CBC with differential
assessment_items.timing: For Downes ≥ 4 or suspicion of infection

items.point: Expiratory grunting is a key RDS sign — it represents auto-PEEP generated by partial glottic closure to maintain FRC.
Grunting, flaring, and retractions (GFR) are the classic triad. Any combination with RR > 60 = distress.
Reassess Downes score every 30 minutes in the first 2 hours. A rising score indicates worsening.

items.annotation: Original Downes Score validation — strong inter-rater reliability in neonatal RD.

routing.question: What is the calculated Downes Score?

clinical_content.summary: Determine most likely etiology for mild respiratory distress to guide targeted management.

criteria.label: CXR: central haziness, fluid in fissures, hyperinflation; C-section delivery; resolving within 24–72h
CXR: ground-glass opacification; GA 34–36 wks; preterm delivery
Meconium-stained amniotic fluid; CXR: patchy infiltrates; coarse, irregular opacification
Maternal fever/chorioamnionitis; elevated CRP/CBC; culture results

items.point: TTN is the most common cause of mild RD in term infants — self-limited, resolves 24–72h.
TTN and RDS cannot always be distinguished clinically — CXR is essential for differentiation.
Never withhold sepsis workup if there is any maternal fever or chorioamnionitis history.

routing.question: What is the most likely etiology based on CXR and clinical context?

branches.label: TTN — Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn
branches.condition: CXR wet-lung pattern + C-section + term GA + improving

branches.label: Probable neonatal pneumonia / sepsis
branches.condition: Maternal fever, chorioamnionitis, or elevated inflammatory markers

clinical_content.summary: Downes 4–6: Initiate CPAP or escalated O2 support; complete diagnostic workup; reassess in 30 minutes.

actions.label: Initiate nasal CPAP at 5–6 cmH2O; titrate FiO2 to maintain SpO2 90–95%.
NPO (nothing by mouth); insert orogastric tube to decompress stomach.
IV fluid: D10W at GIR 6–8 mg/kg/min if unable to feed; UAC/UVC if available.
Obtain CBC, blood culture × 2, CRP, blood gas.
Obtain AP chest X-ray if not yet done.
If infection not excluded: Start empiric ampicillin + gentamicin after cultures.

dosing.notes: Refer to weight-based neonatal dosing chart; adjust for renal function

actions.label: Notify neonatology; consider transfer if no NICU capability.
Reassess Downes score at 30 and 60 minutes.

items.point: Early CPAP reduces surfactant use and mechanical ventilation in RDS (SUPPORT Trial).
If CPAP fails (FiO2 > 0.4 to maintain SpO2), prepare for surfactant administration via INSURE technique.
Temperature maintenance is critical: use servo-controlled warmer or incubator; target 36.5–37.5°C.

items.annotation: SUPPORT trial: early CPAP non-inferior to prophylactic surfactant in near-term RDS.

routing.question: At 30-minute reassessment: Is Downes score improving (decreasing) on CPAP?

branches.label: YES — Improving: Downes score decreasing, SpO2 stable ≥ 90%

clinical_content.summary: Downes 7–10 or failure to respond to CPAP. Prepare for intubation and surfactant. Arrange urgent transfer to Level III NICU.

actions.label: Call for help — neonatologist, most experienced provider available.
Pre-oxygenate with 100% O2 by face mask before intubation.
Intubate — ETT size: [GA/10 + 3.5] cm or weight-based chart. Confirm with CO2 colorimetric detector and CXR.
Administer surfactant (beractant or poractant alfa) via intratracheal route.

dosing.notes: = 4 mL/kg. Give in 2–4 aliquots, repositioning after each. Repeat q6h × 3 doses max if FiO2 > 0.3 needed.

actions.label: Initiate conventional mechanical ventilation: PIP 18–22, PEEP 4–5, RR 40–60, FiO2 to maintain SpO2 90–95%.
Consider INSURE technique (early extubation to CPAP) once surfactant administered and patient stabilizes.
actions.conditional: Neonate spontaneously breathing, improving after surfactant

actions.label: Arrange immediate transport to Level III NICU — call transport team.
Complete transport stabilization bundle: warm, glucose, IV access, monitoring, documentation.

time_constraint.label: Immediate action required
time_constraint.urgency_note: Surfactant should be administered within 2 hours of birth for maximum benefit.

items.point: Surfactant within 2 hours of birth provides maximum benefit in RDS. Delay increases mortality.
INSURE technique reduces duration of mechanical ventilation. Attempt extubation to CPAP as soon as neonate is stable.
During transport, target ventilator settings to maintain PaCO2 45–55 (permissive hypercapnia acceptable in RDS).

items.alert: Avoid hyperventilation (PaCO2 < 35) — associated with periventricular leukomalacia and cerebral vasoconstriction.
Confirm ETT position at lip (weight kg + 6 cm rule) and via CXR before transport.

terminal-ttn.title: TTN — Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn

clinical_content.summary: Confirmed TTN. Supportive care and close monitoring. Expected resolution within 24–72 hours.

items.point: TTN is caused by delayed resorption of fetal lung fluid, not a surfactant deficiency — surfactant is NOT indicated.
Watch for the uncommon TTN mimic: pulmonary hypertension (PPHN). Obtain echo if no improvement by 4–6 hours.
Formula or expressed breast milk feedings can resume when RR < 60/min and stable.

diagnosis.label: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN)
diagnosis.one_liner: Delayed clearance of fetal lung fluid — self-limited, resolves 24–72h with supportive care.

immediate_actions.action: Supplemental O2 by oxyhood or nasal cannula to maintain SpO2 90–95%.
NPO with IV D10W if RR > 60/min — no oral feeds until respiratory rate stable.
Continuous pulse oximetry and cardiorespiratory monitoring.
Reassess RR and Downes score every 1–2 hours.
Advance feeds when RR < 60 and Downes ≤ 2 for 2 consecutive assessments.

monitoring_parameters.escalation_trigger: RR > 80 or not improving by 6 hours

disposition.transport_considerations: Transfer to Level III if FiO2 > 0.4 or no improvement by 6–8 hours.
consult_required: Neonatology if no improvement by 4 hours

clinical_pearls: TTN is a diagnosis of exclusion — CXR and clinical course must be consistent.
Cesarean section at any GA is the #1 risk factor — no vaginal squeeze = retained lung fluid.
Mild TTN may not require supplemental O2 — if SpO2 ≥ 93% in room air with RR < 70, close obs acceptable.
Consider ECHO if no improvement by 4–6 hours to rule out PPHN.
common_pitfalls: Attributing PPHN or CHD to TTN — obtain ECHO if preductal-postductal SpO2 gradient > 10%.
Feeding a neonate with RR > 60 — aspiration risk is high.
Giving surfactant for TTN — not beneficial, not indicated.
Discharging before RR has been stable < 60 for at least 4 hours.
cheatsheet.family_communication: Explain that TTN is a common, temporary breathing adjustment after birth. Expected to resolve on its own within 1–3 days. No long-term lung effects expected.

clinical_content.summary: Mild-to-moderate RDS responding to CPAP therapy. Continue Level II monitoring; have surfactant prepared.

diagnosis.label: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS), Mild — CPAP-Responsive
diagnosis.one_liner: Surfactant deficiency in near-term neonate, improving on CPAP — continue close monitoring and have surfactant immediately available.

immediate_actions.action: Continue CPAP at 5–6 cmH2O; maintain SpO2 90–95% with titrated FiO2.
NPO; IV fluid D10W at 60–80 mL/kg/day.
Surfactant (beractant/poractant) drawn up at bedside — ready for INSURE if FiO2 requirement rises > 0.3.
Serial Downes scoring every 30 minutes × 2 hours, then every hour.
Repeat CXR at 4–6 hours if no improvement.

medications.indication: RDS — surfactant replacement if FiO2 > 0.3 on CPAP or worsening
medications.frequency: May repeat q6h × 3 doses if FiO2 remains > 0.3
medications.preparation: = 4 mL/kg. Warm to room temperature. Administer in 2–4 aliquots.
medications.monitoring: CXR after each dose; monitor SpO2 and FiO2 requirements

monitoring_parameters.escalation_trigger: Score ≥ 7 or acute deterioration → Severe management pathway

monitoring_parameters.frequency: Every 2–4 hours or with clinical change

clinical_pearls: Early CPAP initiation reduces surfactant use and intubation rates (SUPPORT Trial).
INSURE technique: brief intubation → surfactant → rapid extubation to CPAP. Target within 30–60 minutes.
FiO2 > 0.4 on CPAP 6–8 cmH2O = CPAP failure → surfactant + intubation.
Watch for pneumothorax — complication in 5–10% of RDS managed with CPAP.
common_pitfalls: Delaying surfactant when FiO2 threshold reached — earlier is better.
Overtitrating FiO2 above 0.4 before considering surfactant.
Inadequate CPAP pressure — minimum 5 cmH2O; consider 6–7 for moderate RDS.
Not having surfactant drawn up at bedside before CPAP trial.

clinical_content.summary: Severe RDS: intubated, surfactant given, NICU transport initiated. Maintain stabilization bundle during transport.

diagnosis.label: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS), Severe — Intubated
diagnosis.one_liner: Severe RDS requiring intubation and surfactant replacement — stabilized and arranged for Level III NICU transport.

immediate_actions.action: Confirm ETT position: lip mark (weight kg + 6 cm), CO2 detector, CXR (tip at T1–T2).
Ventilator settings: PIP 18–22, PEEP 4–5, RR 40–60, I:E 1:2, FiO2 titrated to SpO2 90–95%.
Repeat surfactant in 6 hours if FiO2 still > 0.3 (max 3–4 doses total).
Glucose: D10W at 80 mL/kg/day; recheck glucose in 1 hour.
Transport documentation: maternal history, delivery events, resuscitation steps, medications given, current settings.
Call receiving NICU with SBAR handoff before transport departure.

medications.indication: Repeat dosing if FiO2 > 0.3 at 6h intervals
medications.frequency: q6h × up to 3 total additional doses

medications.indication: Apnea of prematurity (if extubation to CPAP planned post-surfactant)

monitoring_parameters.frequency: Continuous via UAC or q15 min
monitoring_parameters.escalation_trigger: MAP < GA (weeks) = hypotension → normal saline bolus 10 mL/kg

disposition.transport_considerations: Level III NICU transport team. Ensure transport ventilator settings match current. Bring surfactant supply for repeat dosing en route if needed.

clinical_pearls: Document lip mark of ETT at each reassessment — neonatal ETTs migrate easily.
Avoid inadvertent hyperventilation — target PaCO2 45–55 mmHg (permissive hypercapnia) to protect brain.
Caffeine loading before planned extubation to CPAP improves extubation success rates.
PPHN can complicate severe RDS — suspect if SpO2 gradient preductal vs postductal > 10%.
common_pitfalls: Hyperventilating: PaCO2 < 35 associated with IVH and PVL in neonates.
Failing to confirm ETT position after any repositioning of the infant.
Inadequate thermal protection during transport — hypothermia worsens outcomes.
Forgetting to send family communication and documentation with transport team.
cheatsheet.family_communication: Explain that the baby has a lung condition called RDS, which is caused by immature lungs not making enough surfactant. The baby has received medication to help the lungs and is on a breathing machine. Transfer to the NICU is needed for intensive monitoring and further treatment. Emphasize that the team will stay in contact throughout transport.
